method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase; not independent or human review.
scope: All fifteen translated content blocks on pairing functions, codes and nine exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The inverse zig-zag map sends a pair to its diagonal position; triangular numbers give the closed formula (n+m+1)(n+m)/2+n.
samples.checks: Row/column shift, triangular-number index, formula and example value 7 remain unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An arithmetical pairing function is an injection from A×B into Nat; its value is a numeric code and inversion decodes represented pairs.
samples.checks: Injectivity is retained and not silently strengthened in the definition; coding is not described as encryption.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Exercises enumerate nonnegative rationals, all rationals, finite binary strings, truth functions, finite subsets and finite-or-cofinite subsets.
samples.checks: Signs, fraction denominator, finite scopes, truth-function domain and complement condition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A countable family of countable sets has countable union.
samples.checks: Marathi wording explicitly applies countability both to the index family and to each member set; infinite-union formula unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For a bijective pairing function the inverse is an enumeration; for an arbitrary injective pairing function, the inverse is only defined on its range but still proves A×B countable.
samples.checks: OLSIZ-003 corrects the source exercise without changing its formula inventory; the correction is adjacent and traceable.

limitations: T067-T071 include provisional compositional vocabulary open to correction.
No independent linguistic certification has been performed.
